draft.title: Australia's health status
card: Australians live long lives compared with people in most countries. Australia has one of the highest life expectancies in the world.
Most deaths and illness in Australia are now caused by chronic diseases. These are long-lasting conditions that often develop slowly and last for years.
Common examples are heart disease, cancer and diabetes. Many of them are linked to lifestyle factors, such as diet and physical activity.
So a long life expectancy does not mean few health problems. Many Australians live for years with a chronic disease.
draft.remember: Australians live long, but chronic disease causes most deaths and illness.

a.q: Which statement best describes Australia's health status?
opts: Long life expectancy, but mostly chronic illness
Long life expectancy, but mostly infectious illness
Short life expectancy, and mostly chronic illness
Short life expectancy, and mostly injury deaths
a.why: Australia has one of the highest life expectancies, and chronic diseases such as heart disease, cancer and diabetes cause most deaths and illness. Infectious disease is the tempting wrong option, but it is not the main cause of illness in Australia now.
a.clue: Think about both how long people live and what makes them ill.

b.q: Leila says: "Australians live so long that most people must be in good health until they die." Why is her claim weak?
opts: Many people live for years with a chronic disease
Life expectancy in Australia is lower than in most countries
Chronic diseases are rare causes of death in Australia
Life expectancy only counts deaths from heart disease
b.why: Chronic diseases cause most illness and deaths in Australia, and many people live with them for years. A long life expectancy shows people live to an older age, but it does not show they are free of illness. The option about a low life expectancy is wrong because Australia's is among the highest.
b.clue: Living long and living without illness are different things.

a.best: Long life expectancy, but mostly chronic illness
